thread:
Marco (support): Hey team, escalation from enterprise customer running Redwood Private on their on-prem: streaming SSE connections frequently drop ~25-40s in, producing partial final tokens. They see a client reconnect loop, but the resumed responses are truncated/duplicated. File a quick summary and repro below.

Marco (support): Customer environment: on-prem ingress -> corporate proxy (transparent) -> internal LB -> Redwood Private ingress. MTU on on-prem network is 9000, but proxy enforces 1500. Symptoms seen in their app logs:
```
stream: received data chunk: 'Hello world, this is par'
stream: connection closed unexpectedly (code: EOF)
client: reconnecting, resume_id=abc123
stream: resumed, first chunk: 'Hello world, this is par'
stream: connection closed, partial output
```

Marco (support): They sent us a pcap extract and proxy logs. Proxy shows repeated 502/504 around chunk boundaries and a "request body too large" style stanza when chunk size > 1400 bytes. They also have an edge case where our keepalive (":\n\n") heartbeats get stripped by the proxy.

Liz S (eng-sre): Thanks, Marco. Two quick hypotheses: (1) PMTU / fragmentation + proxy that blocks fragmented responses -> fragments dropped mid-stream causing client-side EOF, (2) proxy implements poor HTTP/1.1 chunking handling or has a buffer threshold that closes idle streaming responses. Both can explain partial outputs and duplicate tokens on reconnect.

Jen R (eng-runtime): Can we get a minimal repro curl command from them? If they can reproduce we can test bypassing proxy or toggling chunk sizes. Example to reproduce raw SSE:
```
curl -v --no-buffer \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://private.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=rlm-large" > sse.out
```
Ask them to run with `--no-buffer` and `--http1.1` to force chunked transfer.

Marco (support): They ran that and attached sse.out and a trimmed pcap. sse.out shows several complete events then a sudden EOF. pcap shows a TCP segment with MSS 1440 followed by a RST from the proxy. Packet sequence:
- server -> client: large data segments, segmented at 1440
- proxy -> server: FIN after 25s
- proxy logs: "client closed unexpectedly" and "body buffer exceeded 131072 bytes"

Omar (devex): If the proxy buffers and then decides to close, client reconnects produce repeated prefixes because our server's resume token behavior replays cached prefix. That explains duplication.

Jen R (eng-runtime): Two immediate things to try for customer: (A) Enable small-chunk mode on our side (max chunk ~1k) so proxy sees smaller segments; (B) Toggle SSE heartbeat frequency to send a 1-2 byte keepalive every 10s to prevent proxy idle buffer flush. We should provide a quick server-side patch and a client-side workaround.

Liz S (eng-sre): Also check MTU/PMTU: if on-prem network MTU is jumbo (9000) while proxy uses 1500, server will fragment at IP layer and many proxies block fragmented responses. Recommend asking them to set their egress to 1500 or enable Path MTU discovery on the proxy.

Marco (support): Customer tried client heartbeat but says the proxy still drops after ~30s. They can repro within 90% of attempts. They provided proxy product/version (CorpProxy 3.2.1) which is known to have a stream buffering behavior when Transfer-Encoding: chunked streams exceed ~128KB.

Jen R (eng-runtime): OK next: collect a small server-side trace with headers we send and timing. Key headers: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, and whether we set `Content-Length` (we don't). Also check that we aren't sending `Connection: close` accidentally. Send them a patched header set to include `Connection: keep-alive` and `Cache-Control: no-transform` to try to stop proxy rewriting.

Marco (support): Provided header dump. It includes `X-Redwood-Stream-Id` and no `Cache-Control`. I asked them to curl with extra header to see if proxy treats the response differently: `-H "Cache-Control: no-transform"`. They said it reduced the frequency of drops but didn't eliminate them.

Liz S (eng-sre): Reasonable. "no-transform" sometimes prevents proxies from buffering/rewriting. But if the proxy enforces an internal buffer limit, only reducing chunk size or bypassing the proxy will fully fix.

Omar (devex): For a temporary customer-facing workaround, recommend: 1) client retry/backoff with idempotent resume tokens (they already have), 2) server send smaller SSE chunks and increase heartbeat frequency to 5s, 3) set `Cache-Control: no-transform` and explicit `Connection: keep-alive`. Provide a small python SSE client that handles duplicates by de-duping resume prefix on resume id.

Marco (support): Customer asked about auth/token expiration mid-stream. Their tokens are long-lived, and we saw no 401s in the logs, so not the cause here. However, if reconnects hit rate limits or billing enforcements, the reconnect can be rejected causing permanent truncation — check account usage during repro.

Jen R (eng-runtime): Action items from runtime:
- Add an opt-in server flag for Private deployments: `--sse-max-chunk-size` (default off) to force smaller chunk writes. Patch ETA: 72h.
- Add `Cache-Control: no-transform` header by default behind our private ingress when `private.proxy_mode=on` is detected. Patch ETA: 5d.
- Instrument metrics for `sse_disconnect_reason` to catch `proxy_reset` vs `client_close` (quick PR).

Liz S (eng-sre): From infra side: provide support steps to customer to test bypass: (1) put a quick nginx reverse proxy that forwards to Redwood and set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1;` — if that eliminates disconnects, the culprit is CorpProxy buffering. Share an nginx example config snippet: 
```
location /v1/stream/ {
  proxy_pass http://redwood-ingress;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_request_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
}
```

Marco (support): Customer tried an nginx bypass inside their network and stream stayed alive for 6+ minutes. So it's confirmed proxy behaviour. They're pushing for a long-term fix because they cannot reconfigure CorpProxy.

Jen R (eng-runtime): Long-term options: document recommended proxy configs to customers and add our own server-side mitigation for Private: chunk-size option and more aggressive heartbeats. Also discuss adding a `X-Redwood-SSE-Bypass` header that our support can include in routes for customers with corporate proxies — but need legal/security review before adding headers that try to influence third-party proxies.

Omar (devex): Also update our docs (DevEx) with an "On-prem streaming troubleshooting" quick checklist: MTU/PMTU, proxy buffering, heartbeat frequency, curl repro, nginx bypass example, and how to provide pcap + header dump.

Marco (support): Customer is ok with the temporary nginx workaround while we land runtime patches. They've requested a reproducible checklist to hand to their network team. I'll send that and keep ticket open.

ops-bot: auto-note: created follow-up ticket INF-7234 assigned to eng-runtime, due 3d.

deploy-bot: patch branch `sse-chunk-size-opt` created for eng-runtime.

Jen R (eng-runtime): I'll raise the PR for the chunk-size flag and add a small integration test that runs a simulated proxy that enforces a 128KB buffer and ensures stream doesn't drop.

Liz S (eng-sre): I'll draft the troubleshooting KB for on-prem and include PMTU checks and an example `tracepath`/`mtu` command for customers.

Marco (support): Great — keeping this thread updated. TL;DR: root cause = corporate proxy buffering + PMTU mismatch. Short-term: nginx bypass or force smaller chunks + heartbeats. Medium-term: runtime opt-in to smaller SSE chunks + docs.

Marco (support): Customer will confirm once runtime patch is deployed in their private bundle. I'll close when they validate. :thumbsup:
